title: B/R Week 3 2026 College Football Winners & Losers: Top Upsets, Surprising Falls Revealed
body:
The third week of the 2026 college football season has already etched itself into the collective memory of fans and analysts alike, delivering a cascade of surprise outcomes that reshaped conference narratives and set the tone for the remainder of the year. While the Miami Hurricanes continued to dominate the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) leaderboard, a fierce challenge emerged from Louisville, whose dramatic victory over SMU signaled that the traditional hierarchy could be more fluid than many expected. Meanwhile, a series of upsets across the Power Five conferences highlighted the growing parity in the sport, prompting pundits to reassess early‑season projections and the true contenders for the national title.

In the ACC, Miami’s 38‑24 triumph over Virginia Tech reaffirmed its status as the conference’s premier program, extending its unbeaten run to 5‑0. The Hurricanes’ balanced attack—anchored by a revitalized rushing game and a quarterback who threw for over 300 yards—demonstrated why they remain the benchmark for ACC excellence. Yet, the real story came from Louisville, which dispatched SMU 31‑27 in a high‑scoring affair that saw the Cardinals’ defense forced into a “defense‑optional” role. Louisville’s quarterback, a sophomore phenom, accounted for four total touchdowns, while the offense’s tempo forced SMU into a hurried, error‑prone rhythm. The win not only marked Louisville’s first victory over a non‑conference opponent this season but also positioned the Cardinals as the most credible threat to Miami’s ACC crown.

The Big Ten and SEC also delivered their share of intrigue. In the Midwest, Ohio State’s 42‑17 rout of Purdue underscored the Buckeyes’ offensive firepower, yet a narrow 28‑24 win over Indiana raised eyebrows about consistency on the line of scrimmage. Meanwhile, the SEC saw Alabama stumble 27‑24 against a revitalized Auburn squad, a result that jolted the Crimson Tide’s early‑season aura of invincibility. Auburn’s aggressive blitz package and a late fourth‑quarter field goal turned the tide, suggesting that the SEC’s “no‑one‑beats‑Alabama” mantra may be eroding faster than anticipated.

Mid‑major programs added further drama to Week 3. Boise State, long regarded as the “blue‑chip” of the Group of Five, suffered a stunning 31‑28 defeat to Nevada, a game decided by a last‑second Hail Mary that left Boise’s fans reeling. Similarly, the Pac‑12’s Washington State secured a 24‑21 victory over Oregon State, leveraging a stout defensive front that forced three turnovers in the second half. These outcomes highlight a broader trend: the gap between Power Five and Group of Five teams is narrowing, and the ability to execute under pressure is becoming the new differentiator.

Analysts are already interpreting these results through the lens of “prisoners of the moment” – a phrase that captures the danger of overvaluing early‑season performances while ignoring the volatility inherent in college football. The consensus that Miami sits atop the ACC is now tempered by Louisville’s emergence, and the early dominance of traditional powerhouses like Alabama and Ohio State is being questioned by the resilience of underdogs. Moreover, the week’s defensive lapses—particularly in high‑scoring contests such as Louisville vs. SMU—suggest that coaching staffs may need to adapt their schemes to counter increasingly versatile offenses.

Looking ahead, the implications of Week 3 will reverberate through the rest of the season. If Louisville sustains its offensive momentum, the ACC could witness its first genuine intra‑conference power struggle in over a decade, forcing Miami to tighten its defensive schemes and perhaps rethink its recruiting priorities. In the SEC, Alabama’s stumble may serve as a catalyst for strategic adjustments, especially in secondary coverage, as opponents have already begun to exploit previously unseen vulnerabilities. Finally, the tightening competition between Power Five and Group Five programs could lead to more high‑stakes non‑conference matchups, enriching the overall landscape of college football.

As the schedule progresses, fans and commentators alike will be watching closely to see whether Week 3’s surprises are isolated anomalies or the harbinger of a more unpredictable, fiercely contested season. One thing is certain: the early narratives have been upended, and the road to the College Football Playoff will be anything but straightforward.
